families.source: UKHSA emergency preparedness, resilience and response collection
families.topic: the agency-wide concept of operations, preparedness plan, incident response plan and supporting annexes
families.page_title: Emergency preparedness, resilience and response: concept of operations
evidence_points: The collection describes UKHSA’s systematic approach to preparing for, responding to and recovering from health-security incidents.
It covers infectious, pandemic, chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear and adverse-weather threats.
It includes the concept of operations, preparedness plan and incident response plan.
It includes accountability, principles and incident-role annexes.
The framework applies across UKHSA.
It supports UKHSA’s Category 1 responder and health-security responsibilities.
The page is an official GOV.UK source for the agency-wide concept of operations, preparedness plan, incident response plan and supporting annexes and was live-checked on 31 July 2026.
The source should be used with current setting-specific, incident-specific and specialist arrangements where applicable.

families.page_title: Emergency preparedness, resilience and response concept of operations
evidence_points: The concept of operations provides the strategic framework for UKHSA preparedness, response and recovery.
It uses an all-threats approach covering natural, accidental and malicious hazards.
It explains UKHSA responsibilities under the Civil Contingencies Act and as a DHSC executive agency.
It links the strategic framework to preparedness, incident-response and threat-specific plans.
It describes risk-based escalation from routine to more severe response arrangements.
Co-operation, business continuity and recovery are part of the framework.

families.topic: preparing people, plans and infrastructure and assessing readiness through an annual preparedness cycle
evidence_points: The plan describes how UKHSA prepares people, plans and infrastructure for health-security incidents.
It covers routine incidents and nationally coordinated standard, enhanced and severe arrangements.
Preparedness is directed by risk assessment and agreed objectives.
Plans are consulted on, issued, trained, exercised, maintained and reviewed.
The annual preparedness cycle connects prioritised threats to readiness assessment and resource planning.
Incident roles require appropriate competence, training and continuing development.

evidence_points: The plan is an all-hazards framework for significant public-health and business-continuity incidents.

It describes incident-response levels and escalation or de-escalation parameters.

evidence_points: The Chief Executive is accountable for UKHSA outcomes during a health-security incident.
